bremner-theorem1-proof-gate-set: Proof of Theorem 1, p.7 to p.8: the paper states the gate set (H, Z, CZ, P = e^{i pi/8 Z}) and that all are 1- or 2-qubit gates and, apart from H, have diagonal entries that are integer powers of e^{i pi/8}. That is the proof's own stated setup. Universality of the set is taken as standard background; the value only repeats the paper's phrase.
bremner-theorem3-log-output-sampling: Theorem 3, Section 3.2, p.10, with its condition (uniform IQP family, output registers of size O(log n)). The proof is complete in the paper (p.10 to p.11): the Z-basis form gives the state of eq. (9), the phase f(x,y) is computed in poly(n) time, Y_w is uniformly random, and the remaining O(log n)-qubit state is simulated exactly. It uses no other paper's theorem as a step.
bremner-theorem3-proof-method: Proof of Theorem 3, p.10 to p.11: these are the steps of a complete proof the paper gives (phase function in poly(n) time; uniform measurement of Y_w; direct strong simulation of the O(log n)-qubit state). Graded with Theorem 3, which is HIGH.
bremner-def1-uniform-family: Definition 1, Section 2.2, p.3: the paper defines a uniform family of circuits. The value matches the quote and the passage.
bremner-def2-iqp-circuit: Definition 2, Section 2.3, p.4: the paper defines an IQP circuit. The value matches the quote.
bremner-iqp-gate-specification-conventio: Section 2.3, p.4: the paper states its convention (gates given by diagonal entries and lines) and that other conventions exist, e.g. [4]. The O(log n) consequence is immediate from a poly(n) description. A statement of what the paper covers.
bremner-iqp-z-basis-representation: Section 2.3, p.4: the paper defines the Z-basis representation (each line starts and ends with H, every gate between is diagonal in Z) and gives the equivalence argument in the same paragraph (insert HH, absorb the H's into conjugations). The argument is short and complete.
bremner-def-bpp-pp-bqp: Section 2.2, p.4: the paper defines BPP, PP and BQP by uniform families of circuits. The value matches the two quotes in context.
bremner-def3-post-iqp: Definition 3, Section 2.4, p.5: the paper defines post-IQP (and post-BQP, post-BPP) with conditions (i) and (ii). Single-line output register and a poly-size post-selection register match the passage. Eq. (1) requires non-zero post-selection probability; the value omits that but says nothing wrong.
bremner-post-selection-overhead: Section 2.4, p.5: the paper states that post-selection may incur an exponential overhead and is mainly a theoretical tool, not a feasible resource. That caveat applies to its post-IQP construction. A limit the paper states about its own work.
bremner-def-strong-simulation: Section 2.5 (a), p.6: the paper defines strong simulability. The value matches the quote.
bremner-def-weak-simulation: Section 2.5 (b), p.6: the paper defines weak simulability. The value matches the quote.
bremner-def-weak-simulation-multiplicati: Section 2.5 (c), p.6: the paper defines weak simulability with multiplicative error c. The bounds 1/c prob[P=x] <= prob[R=x] <= c prob[P=x] are eq. (2), read from the fragmented text layer and consistent with the value.
bremner-def-weak-simulation-tv-distance: Section 2.5 (d), p.6: the paper defines weak simulability within epsilon total variation distance, with eq. (2) replaced by the sum of |prob[P=x] - prob[R=x]| < epsilon. The value matches.
bremner-def-weak-simulation-additive-pol: Section 2.5 (e), p.6: the paper states 'We say that a circuit family is ... weakly simulatable with additive polynomial error if ...'. The notion comes from [11] but the paper defines the term in its own text.
bremner-def-polynomial-hierarchy: Section 3.1, p.7: the paper defines PH as the union of the tower Delta_k with Delta_1 = P and Delta_{k+1} = P^{N Delta_k}. The value matches.

theory_low.bremner-abstract-collapse-to-third-level: Abstract, p.1 summarizes Corollary 1. That corollary is itself LOW (it rests on Aaronson's post-BQP = PP [6] and Han et al. [16]). The abstract adds no proof.
theory_low.bremner-theorem1-post-iqp-equals-pp: Theorem 1, p.7. The proof (p.7 to p.8) shows post-IQP = post-BQP by the Hadamard gadget. The step post-BQP = PP is Aaronson's theorem [6], cited in Section 3.1 ('Aaronson[6] has shown that post-BQP=PP'), not proved here. The gadget calculation is also called 'easy' and not printed. A proof that uses another paper's theorem as a step is LOW: Aaronson, post-BQP = PP.
theory_low.bremner-theorem1-proof-gadget: p.8: the paper says 'An easy calculation shows' and does not print it. A proof step asserted, not shown. Part of Theorem 1, which is LOW.
theory_low.bremner-theorem1-proof-swap: p.8: one sentence asserts that SWAP gates can be commuted to the end of the lines. No derivation is given. Part of Theorem 1, which is LOW.
theory_low.bremner-theorem1-nearest-neighbour-2d: p.9: a remark argued in a few lines from Figure 1(b), with no formal proof ('logically speaking'). Not a proved result.
theory_low.bremner-theorem2-post-bpp-equals-pp: Theorem 2, p.9. The proof ends 'theorem 1 ... will give post-BPP = PP'. It therefore depends on Theorem 1, and so on Aaronson's post-BQP = PP [6]. It also takes the independence of post-IQP from the error level from Theorem 1. The text layer drops the square root sign in 'c < 2' (the theorem reads c < sqrt 2). A proof that uses another paper's theorem is LOW: Aaronson, post-BQP = PP.
theory_low.bremner-theorem2-proof-bound-on-c: p.10: the algebra c^2 < 1+2delta is shown, but letting delta approach 1/2 relies on the independence of post-IQP from the error level, which the paper takes from Theorem 1 (LOW, rests on Aaronson [6]). The quote also loses the square root in 'c < 2' in the text layer. Graded with Theorem 2.
theory_low.bremner-theorem2-multiplicative-vs-addit: p.10: an informal explanation in words of why multiplicative error suits the method. No counterexample or proof that additive or TV error fails. A claim of absence argued informally.
theory_low.bremner-corollary1-ph-collapse: Corollary 1, p.10. Its proof uses Theorem 2 (LOW), Toda's theorem [9], and eq. (3), which rests on post-BPP in Delta 3 from Han, Hemaspaandra and Thierauf [16], cited. A proof that uses a specific other paper's result as a step is LOW: Han et al. [16] (post-BPP in Delta 3) and, through Theorem 1, Aaronson [6].
theory_low.bremner-restricted-gate-family-suffices: p.10: a consequence the authors draw 'from the proof of theorem 1' by inspection, with no separate proof. Theorem 1 is itself LOW.
theory_low.bremner-bppiqp-logn-equals-bpp: p.11: 'it is easy to see' that BPP^IQP is in BQP, and the equality with BPP is stated as following from Theorem 3 with no proof. Stated, not proved.
theory_low.bremner-section4-only-theorem1-needed: Section 4, p.11: an informal generalization. It rests on Theorem 1 and Corollary 1, both LOW here. No formal theorem.
theory_low.bremner-qnc0-conclusion-applies: Section 4, p.11: post-BQNC0 = PP comes from the constructions of [13, 14] (Terhal and DiVincenzo; Fenner et al.), cited, with no proof here. Cited result.
theory_low.bremner-post-iqp-epsilon-independence: Section 2.4, p.5: the independence of post-IQP from epsilon is said to follow from Theorem 1, which is LOW. The second half (BIQP_epsilon not known to be independent) is an open point, not a result. Graded by the weaker part.
theory_low.bremner-simulation-implies-bpp: Section 2.5, p.6 to p.7: stated as an immediate consequence ('will also imply') with a one-line reason about bounded error. No proof is given.
theory_low.bremner-eq3-p-post-bpp-in-delta3: Section 3.1, p.7: eq. (3) uses post-BPP in Delta 3 from Han, Hemaspaandra and Thierauf [16], cited and not proved here, plus P^(P^C) = P^C argued in one line. A cited result is LOW: Han et al. [16].
